name: Wulwulam
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog (Harvey 2003): language attested only in a short wordlist

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2003. Bininj Gun-Wok: a pan-dialectal grammar of Mayali, Kunwinjku and Kune. Pacific Linguistics 541 (Glottolog ref 701876, cited for Wulwulam at pp. 32-35).
sources.note: pp. 32-35 give the Gunwinyguan family tree (Fig. 1.8) and the western subgroup 'Warray and Jawoyn'; Wulwulam is not named anywhere in the volume (a full-text search for stress/accent). Its phonology chapter is about Bininj Gun-wok, not Wulwulam.

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 1986. Ngoni Waray Amungal-yang: the Waray language from Adelaide River. MA thesis, Australian National University.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Describes Warray stress. Relevant only if Wulwulam is judged a Warray dialect (Harvey's first hypothesis, 'cannot be resolved'); Harvey and Glottolog both treat it as a separate language, so a Warray statement should not be transferred to wulw1234.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for Wulwulam [wulw1234] and reference records 701876, 414352, 122222, 661045.
sources.note: States the language is 'attested only in a short wordlist but this wordlist is not explainable as Warray or any other neighbouring language'; lists only Evans 2003 pp. 32-35, Harvey 2003 pp. 295-299 (wordlist), Evans & Marley 2023 p. 783. No descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference exists.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Warray language' (the 'Wulwulam language' title redirects here).
sources.note: Says only 'Wulwulam (Worrwolam) may have been a dialect. Ngorrkkowo may have been another name for Wulwulam.' Its phonology and Tryon 1968 wordlist are Warray, not Wulwulam.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas (ed.). 2003. The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia. Pacific Linguistics 552 (full volume, CC BY-SA 4.0 online edition 2015).
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent Wulwulam/Wolwolam/Ngorrkgowo: all hits are in Harvey's ch. 10 (above). No stress statement for Wulwulam anywhere in the volume.

sources.citation: Harvey, Mark. 2003. Western Gunwinyguan. In Nicholas Evans (ed.), The non-Pama-Nyungan languages of northern Australia: comparative studies of the continent's most linguistically complex region, 285-303. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 552. §3 'Wulwulam' pp. 295-299 (= Glottolog ref 414352 'Wulwulam', document type wordlist; chapter = Glottolog ref 122222).
sources.note: Nothing about Wulwulam stress. §3 presents the only material on the language: a 28-item wordlist from Baldwin Spencer's 1912 field notes (Table 12, p. 296) 'with putative phonological and morphological analysis'; no verbs, no prosody. The chapter's single stress remark (p. 291: AnpekkoLa, AnporrokkorL 'have a single primary stress on their second syllable.. Four-syllable nouns consisting solely of an unanalysable root normatively have stresses on the first and third syllables') concerns Warray place names, not Wulwulam.

sources.citation: Spencer, Baldwin. 1914. Native tribes of the Northern Territory of Australia. London: Macmillan (pp. 6-7, 179, 199-200 name the 'Wulwullam' / Pine Creek tribe).
sources.note: Ethnography only (tribe list, moieties, totems: 'The Pine Creek or Wulwullam tribe is now decadent', p. 199). No language data; the wordlist is in Spencer's unpublished 1912 field notes, not in this book.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas & Alexandra Marley. 2023. The Gunwinyguan languages. In Claire Bowern (ed.), The Oxford Guide to Australian Languages, 781-795. Oxford University Press.

sources.note: Latest handbook treatment cited by Glottolog for Wulwulam (p. 783); would only confirm the classification and that no further material has surfaced since 2003. Cannot contain a stress statement for a 28-word list.

sources.citation: Spencer, W. Baldwin. 1912. Field notes (Pine Creek, 'Wailwullam' vocabulary, c. 2 pages). Manuscript, Museum Victoria, Melbourne.

sources.note: The sole primary record of Wulwulam (28 items). Only conceivable place a stress mark could exist, and Spencer's amateur transcription almost certainly carries none; Harvey 2003 already published the list in full.
